data.label: Synthetic sensor event generator
data.description: Existing synthetic event producer, outside the provisioning scope. It sends JSON events with device_id, event timestamp, metric, value and unit.

data.label: Ingestion topic
data.description: Pub/Sub topic and subscription that durably buffer events with retention, so they can be replayed. The publisher authenticates with a scoped service account. device_id is the ordering key.

data.label: Validation & feature window
data.description: Validates the schema, unit whitelist and timestamp sanity, and keeps device_id, event time and unit unchanged. It builds per-device windows for scoring and sends rejected events to the dead-letter topic with a reason.

data.label: Rejected events (dead-letter)
data.description: Dead-letter topic for invalid or unprocessable events, kept for inspection and replay.

data.label: Anomaly scoring model
data.description: Returns an anomaly score and flag for each device window. In local tests it is a scripted mock. The real model, its training labels and its thresholds are not decided yet.

data.label: Anomaly results
data.description: Results table with device_id, event timestamp, unit, value, score, flag and model version, partitioned by event date.

data.label: Operator alerting
data.description: Raises an alert from a log-based metric on flagged anomalies. It also alerts on dead-letter backlog and pipeline lag.

data.label: Operator
data.description: Existing on-call person who receives alerts through an email or chat notification channel that is still to be confirmed.

lastAsked.question: How much history do you have for what you want to predict?
lastAsked.beginner: For example “three years of sales by store” or “failure records since 2020”.
lastAsked.why: It shapes the Predictive ML design.

requirements.statement: Every accepted event and result must keep the original device_id, event timestamp and unit unchanged from ingestion to the results table.
requirements.rationale: If identity or units are lost, alerts can point to the wrong device or misread values.
requirements.basis: User: "Preserve device identity, timestamps and units."

requirements.statement: Invalid events go to a dead-letter topic with a rejection reason. They are never silently dropped, and a growing backlog alerts the operator.
requirements.rationale: Without this, bad data either corrupts scores or disappears unnoticed.
requirements.basis: User asked for validation, durable buffering and an operator alert.

requirements.statement: Proposed: before go-live, check the anomaly model on a time-based holdout with labelled anomalies and set acceptable detection and false-alarm rates. Mocked model tests are not evidence of model quality.
requirements.rationale: Too many false alarms will lead operators to ignore alerts, and missed anomalies defeat the purpose.
requirements.basis: User: "distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation".

decisions.subject: design.gcp-sensor-anomaly-detection-first-end-to-end-sketch
decisions.title: GCP sensor anomaly detection – first end-to-end sketch
decisions.context: Scope: synthetic sensor events → Pub/Sub (durable buffer) → Dataflow validation (schema check that keeps device_id, timestamp and unit; rejected events go to a dead-letter topic) → Vertex AI online endpoint (anomaly score) → BigQuery results → Cloud Monitoring alert to an existing operator. Assumptions: the region is not chosen yet; the model is a placeholder until we agree on labels and evaluation; local tests use a mocked model. Native Terraform for these GCP services is not generated yet, so engineering work is still needed. Nothing has been deployed or verified.
